entities.name: The Buddhist Mahayana Corpora
entities.label: Text
entities.summary:
The Buddhist Mahayana Corpora encompasses the vast body of scriptures, philosophical treatises, and commentaries of the Mahayana ("Great Vehicle") tradition — the form of Buddhism practiced by the majority of Buddhists worldwide (approximately 350 million across East Asia, Tibet, Mongolia, and Vietnam). Unlike the Pali Canon's closed corpus, the Mahayana literary tradition is open-ended, with new sutras appearing over centuries (c.

100 BCE–700 CE), each claiming to preserve hidden teachings of the Buddha. Key texts include: the Prajnaparamita Sutras (Perfection of Wisdom), particularly the Heart Sutra and Diamond Sutra — among the most recited texts in all of Buddhism; the Lotus Sutra (Saddharmapundarika) — the most influential sutra in East Asian Buddhism; the Avatamsaka Sutra (Flower Garland) — the grandest cosmic vision in Buddhist literature; and Nagarjuna's Mulamadhyamakakarika — the philosophical foundation of Madhyamaka ("Middle Way") thought on emptiness (shunyata).

The corpus is preserved in Chinese (Taisho Tripitaka, 85+ volumes) and Tibetan (Kangyur and Tengyur, 325+ volumes) canons.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: The Buddhist Mahayana Corpora played a crucial role in shaping East Asian Buddhism and influenced the development of numerous philosophical schools, including Chan/Zen and Pure Land. With over 350 million adherents worldwide, its impact on regional culture and spirituality is profound.
